$comment: Generated from Rust deserialization types by game schema. Do not edit. Runtime semantic validators additionally check ranges, references, formats and capabilities.

AnimationData.description:
Skeletal animation state an entity publishes for a host to play.

The engine stores which clip is selected and since which frame; it does not
evaluate bones, meshes or blending. The only declared asset kind for this
today is Spine, and the host owns that runtime.

AudioCategory.description:
How a game groups its sounds, and what the engine does about the grouping.

The engine does not name `bgm` or `sfx`: the taxonomy is the game's. It owns
only the rules, because they decide which source survives a switch, and that
is world state a test asserts.

The reserved fields exist so the declaration shape does not have to change
when they are implemented. Declaring one is an **error**, never a silent
no-op: a game believing it configured something it did not is the hardest
kind of audio bug to find.

exclusive.description:
Only one loop in this category plays at a time; starting another begins
stopping the previous one.

volume.description:
The bus level this category starts at, the way a mixer group has a
volume before anything plays. A settings screen changes it at runtime.

view_height.description:
World units visible vertically at zoom 1, centred on `position`.

Without this a host cannot know how much world a frame shows, so every
host invented its own constant and the same scene framed differently in
each one. The visible height is `view_height / zoom`, and the visible
width is that times the host's viewport aspect.

curvature.description:
Bends world geometry around the target point: in view space relative to
the target, y -= curvature * (x^2 + z^2). 0 disables it.

handedness.description:
How world coordinates map to the screen. `left` keeps x right, y up and
z away from the viewer at identity, as in Direct3D and Unity.

rect.description:
Normalized viewport (lower-left origin) the view renders into; None is
the whole surface.

DataAssetDecl.description:
One data asset a project declares: where the host finds its bytes and which
loader turns them into a Luau value.

loader.description: The manifest's `encoding.decoder`, or "bytes" without an encoding.

source.description: Project-relative path; exports serve it under `content/`.

HostTimeTape.description:
Schema 1 is runtime-creation-origin, floor elapsed milliseconds, safe integer.
Epoch labels are identities supplied by the recording host, never OS uptime.

importers.description:
Importer name -> a node of a project Luau module. This is where a game
adds formats; the engine needs no change for a new source format.

roots.description:
Read-only directories outside the project that imports read, such as an
original game installation the project may not redistribute.

candidates.description:
Directories tried in order (${VAR} expands environment variables) when
the machine-local .unone/import-roots.json does not name this root.

module.description: Project-relative Luau module returning node definitions.

ground_friction.description:
Horizontal velocity lost per second while a body rests on the ground.

Without it a landed body slides the length of the level, which silently
turns a miss into a hit.

linear_damping.description:
Velocity lost per second by every dynamic body, as a fraction.

Defaults to none, which is what this engine simulated before the field
existed: a body keeps its velocity forever unless something takes it.

audio.description:
Sound categories and the rules between them.

Undeclared means no rules, not no sound: a game can still play and loop
without ever naming a category. Categories exist to say what happens
*between* sounds, which is the part the engine owns.

host_time.description: Explicit opt-in demand-sampled host time; absent keeps deterministic legacy behavior.

import.description: Importers and read-only import roots for assets declaring `import`.

job_scripts.description: Isolated Luau job modules, keyed by operation name.

render_pipeline.description:
Ordered render passes the official hosts execute (ADR 0048). Undeclared
keeps each host's built-in order.

runtime_packages.description:
Exact versions of SDK-bundled Luau runtime packages used by this project.
Declare @unone/ui before using api.ui.components constructors. This is
compatibility data, not a network resolver or filesystem module loader.

systems.description:
Engine systems this game explicitly turns on or off.

Anything not declared keeps the engine default; the engine rejects
unknown ids instead of treating a typo as a disabled system.

ui_previews.description:
Screens `verify` must check the layout of.

Without this only the opening screen is ever drawn, so a broken win or
lose screen passes every gate. Each entry says how to reach a screen,
the same way `test_files` says how to reach a state worth asserting.

verify.description:
Which gates `verify` runs, in what order, and which of them are
advisory.

Undeclared means the engine's default order with every gate required.

id.description: Stable name game code uses with api.render.setPass.

params.description: Kind-specific settings; absent ones use the host default.

version.description: Contract version; 1 is the only one.

rotation.description: Visual-only 2D rotation in radians around the sprite centre.

scale.description: Visual-only 2D scale applied to the sprite's declared size.

sprite_animation.description: Fixed-tick frame animation over the sprite's sheet cells.

camera.description:
The one authoring entry point for the active camera. Legacy 2D and
split `camera3d` input is still accepted by the custom deserializer,
but the generated schema advertises the unified forms first.

oneOf.description: Orthographic projection. `orthographicSize` is the visible world height; `position` may be Vec2 or Vec3 (z is ignored).

camera3d.description:
Legacy split perspective storage. New source files should put the
projection in `camera`; this field is accepted only for compatibility
and is intentionally omitted by canonical serialization.

ScriptBytecodeDecl.description: Declares the precompiled entry script in a host payload in place of `script`.

format.description: Compiler identity; must equal the loading runtime's `script_bytecode_format`.

source.description: Content-relative file the host fetches and stages as SCRIPT_BYTECODE_DATA_ID.

ShaderAttribute.description: A named per-vertex input of 1..4 floats.

oneOf.description: The triangle's provoking (last) vertex value everywhere.

ShaderMaterialDefinition.description:
A declared material: the stages and the interface between mesh data, the
vertex stage and the fragment stage. Sprites use only the fragment stage.

attributes.description:
Extra floats each vertex of a mesh using this material carries after
its color, in this order; the vertex stage reads them by name.

fragment.description: GLSL ES 1.00 function: vec4 unoneShade(vec2 uv, vec4 color).

samplers.description: Texture inputs of both stages: lookup tables, palettes, data maps.

varyings.description: Values passed from the vertex stage to the fragment stage by name.

vertex.description:
GLSL ES 3.00 function `vec4 unoneVertex(vec3 position, mat4 model)`
returning the clip-space position. Only geometry3d meshes have a vertex
stage, so a material declaring one cannot shade sprites.

ShaderSampler.description: A texture input of both mesh stages. Unbound samplers read zero.

oneOf.description: `sampler2D`: image assets and rgba8/float data textures.
`isampler2D`: r32i/rgba32i data textures, read exactly with texelFetch.
A runtime data texture (`api.texture`), bound with `api.shader.setTexture`.

ShaderVarying.description: A value of 1..4 floats the vertex stage writes and the fragment stage reads.

SpriteAnimationData.description:
A clip of sprite sheet cells the engine steps on the fixed tick.

The engine resolves the current cell into `sprite.frame` every observation,
so hosts only map a cell to texture coordinates and replays stay exact.

fps.description: Cells per second of fixed-tick time.

frames.description:
Sheet cells in play order, numbered from 0 left to right, then top to
bottom. A cell may repeat to hold it longer.

frame.description:
Sheet cell to draw, numbered from 0 left to right, then top to bottom.
While a sprite animation plays, observations carry its current cell.

layer.description:
Painter layer. Lower layers are drawn first; same-layer order is the
ascending entity id, which is the portable tie-break used by hosts.

sheet.description: Splits the texture into equal cells so the sprite draws one of them.

SpriteSheet.description: A grid of equally sized cells covering the whole texture.

rotation.description:
Euler rotation in radians. The engine stores the transform; game code
owns the meaning of steering and other gameplay-specific orientation.

UiPreviewSpec.description: One reachable screen the layout gate should inspect.

input_sequence.description: Project-relative per-frame input replay that reaches this screen.

overlap_policy.description: Project-relative exact image-behind-control overlap policy for this preview.

save_fixture.description:
Tool-only project-relative JSON save restored before Game.start.
Omitted from serialized/exported project payloads and production files.

VerifyConfig.description:
The gates this project wants `verify` to run.

The default order is the engine's opinion, not a law. A project that draws
no screen, or that is mid-way through acquiring assets, should be able to
say so once in its config rather than teaching its author to read past a
red line — a gate people learn to ignore is worse than a gate that says it
is advisory.

command.description:
Reserved: a project-owned command as a gate. Declaring it is an error in
this build rather than a step that silently never runs.

required.description: A failing advisory gate is reported and does not fail the run.

VerifyStepSpec.description: One declared gate: either the bare id, or the id with its settings.

asset_catalog.description: Declared presentation assets; bytes and decoded/GPU objects stay in the host.

data_assets.description:
Data assets the game reads with api.assets.load. The host delivers their
bytes beside this JSON (into_runtime_with_data), never inside it.

restored_save.description: Restored state is available in Game.start, never injected after startup.

script.description: Entry script source; empty when `script_bytecode` declares a precompiled chunk.

script_bytecode.description:
Precompiled entry script in place of `script`. Its bytes travel beside this
JSON as staged data SCRIPT_BYTECODE_DATA_ID, never inside it.

viewport_aspect.description:
UI viewport aspect, supplied before Game.start; defaults to 16:9.
Ignored when viewport_size is present: the physical size then defines
the aspect exactly, so hosts may send a rounded CSS aspect alongside it.

viewport_size.description: Physical render-target pixels, supplied before Game.start when known.
